_what: What the daily popularity sweep should count each graded server by.
_evidence_standard: A mapping is recorded ONLY when the source's own record points back at the
graded server's hostname. A name that merely looks right is not evidence.
A wrong mapping publishes a stranger's download count under this server's
name, with a timestamp and a trend, and looks exactly like a correct one.
Checked against the live sources on 2026-09-11. Apply with:
Three of 26 graded servers could be mapped. That is the honest yield: most
of the graded set are hosted remote servers with no npm package and no
public repo that names them. Every unmapped server reports
sources_measured: 0, which is the correct output rather than a useful one.

verified.subject: idosal/git-mcp
verified.evidence: GitHub repo record names gitmcp.io. The repo IS the service.

verified.subject: exa-labs/exa-mcp-server
verified.evidence: GitHub repo record names mcp.exa.ai. The repo IS the server.

verified.subject: subwayinfo
verified.evidence: Smithery list row homepage is https://subwayinfo.nyc, verified=true. Moved 16873 -> 22961 between 04:04 and 21:50 on 2026-09-11, so this one already has something to trend.

_declined.subject: withastro/docs
why_declined: It passes the host check: the withastro/docs repo record names
mcp.docs.astro.build. It was still declined, because those stars
measure the Astro DOCS PROJECT and not the MCP server served from
it. An evidenced mapping can still count the wrong population, and
that is a failure the host check is structurally unable to see.
One wrong number carrying a confident trend costs the feed more
credibility than three right ones buy it.
DO NOT re-propose this without new evidence that separates the
server's own popularity from the docs project's. Re-raising it on
the same evidence is re-litigating a settled decision.
